transit_more_other: The Utah transit rail system (Trax & Frontrunner) is way too inconvenient. The idea of park & ride stations is ridiculous - if I have to drive to the station, I might as well just drive to my destination. It's faster to do that, even with traffic. Also, there are only so many directions you can go on the trains, mostly North/South. Big cities like New York and London have successful systems because there are many stations and many directions, so it's easy to get from any point in the city to another. London's underground (""""Tube"""") is laid out like a spider web - North/South, East/West, tons of diagonals (NW/SE, etc.,) and a circle line to connect them all. When I lived in London I used the underground all the time. But I almost never use the rail in Salt Lake. Its just not worth the time and effort. <br/>Also, I think rail travel would be much faster and more efficient if it was underground, instead of the way it is now. I know it would cost a lot to build a subway system, but if a better payment system was installed, UTA could earn the money to at least start paying for such changes. Using the """"honor system"""" for buying a rail ticket is not working. (People cheat ALL the time. It's too easy to ride the trax and front runner without paying for a ticket, and even if someone gets caught, they can just hop on the next train and likely not get caught.) <br/>One can't even reach the train platform in London or New York without purchasing a ticket or having a pre-purchased pass. You need one to be able to go through the gate to the platform. I think UTA is losing a lot of money by using the honor system.<br/>If an efficient payment method could help fund installing many more rail lines, to the point of making rail travel convenient, instead of a hassle, I would be happy to take a train to work and save gas. But with how inefficient our current system is to get where I need to go, it's just not worth it for me.
